papers.title: SMALL AND SICK NEWBORN CARE: LEARNING FOR IMPLEMENTATION ACROSS AFRICA AND BEYOND: Supplement 2
papers.abstract: Background: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) reduces neonatal mortality and morbidity among preterm and low birthweight (LBW) infants, but implementation and quality vary across sub-Saharan African (SSA) hospitals. This study reports KMC coverage and quality of care for preterm and LBW neonates admitted to hospitals in the NEST360 Alliance (Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Nigeria) and examines the association between KMC provision and survival to discharge. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study using routinely collected neonatal inpatient data from hospitals participating in the NEST360 Alliance. Newborns weighing under 2500g were eligible for KMC and included in coverage and quality analyses (January 2021-December 2024). Quality-of-care cascades quantified attrition along the KMC care pathway from eligibility to successful delivery, defining quality as the proportion of eligible neonates reaching each successive step. Mixed-effects logistic regression assessed the association between KMC and survival at discharge, including variation by illness severity and, among KMC recipients, by timing of initiation across severity and birthweight strata. Results: Of 375,238 neonatal admissions across 66 hospitals, 125,844 neonates were eligible for KMC and had KMC documentation available. Among these, 64,619 (51.3%) received KMC. All four countries showed improved coverage over the study period, with the largest absolute increases in Nigeria (27.6%) and Tanzania (27.4%). Excluding Kenya, where KMC timing data were unavailable, 92.1% of neonates started on KMC had a documented start date; of these 44,264 neonates, 12,934 (29.2%) were initiated on KMC on the first day of life. The quality cascade showed eligible neonates were lost at each step, from eligibility through to documented, timely, and sustained KMC. Among neonates eligible for both KMC and CPAP, 39.4% of those started on KMC also received documented CPAP at some point during admission. After adjustment for patient-level factors, receiving KMC was associated with improved survival across all severity groups, with the greatest absolute benefit among the most critically ill neonates (adjusted predicted survival 7% vs 80% without and with KMC, respectively). Conclusion: KMC coverage improved substantially across NEST360-implementing hospitals between 2021 and 2024, demonstrating progress in implementation. However, important gaps remain in the quality and timeliness of KMC delivery. More investment in high-quality KMC implementation, supported by robust monitoring systems linked with quality improvement, are essential to improve outcomes for small and sick newborns across sub-Saharan Africa.

papers.title: Effect of results-based financing on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda: a comparative interrupted time series analysis
papers.abstract: Background Uganda continues to experience a high burden of maternal and child morbidity and mortality, partly due to suboptimal utilization and quality of reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health services. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Health of Uganda, with World Bank funding, implemented results-based financing (RBF) through the Uganda Reproductive, Maternal, and Child Health Services Improvement Project (URMCHIP) in selected districts. Although RBF has been implemented for nearly a decade, evidence on its impact on maternal and child health service indicators in Uganda remains limited. This study assessed the effect of RBF on selected maternal and child health indicators in Mayuge District, Uganda. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the records between July 2018 and June 2019 as the pre-intervention period, July 2019 to June 2021 as the intervention period, and July 2021 to June 2023 as the post-intervention period. We conducted multiple-group interrupted time-series analyses to compare trends in selected maternal and child health indicators between four intervention and three non-intervention health facilities. Results After the implementation of RBF, the number of births in the intervention facilities increased by 1.67 births per month (95% CI [0.19, 3.16]) as compared to the control facilities. The number of women receiving modern family planning methods in intervention facilities increased by 34.1 women per month (CI [25.8, 42.4] as compared to the control facilities. The number of children under five years seen at the outpatient department slightly decreased by -0.24 children per month (CI [-9.58, 9.10]). There was a decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods following the discontinuation of results-based financing in the intervention health facilities. Conclusions There was an improvement in selected maternal and child health indicators in the intervention health facilities following the implementation of RBF, with a subsequent decline in facility-based births and the number of clients receiving modern family planning methods after RBF was discontinued. We recommend that policymakers consider allocating additional funds towards RBF to improve health service delivery.

papers.title: Multidimensional deprivation and brain health in older adults in rural northern Tanzania: a cross-sectional community-based study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Dementia and late-life depression are rising rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, yet prevention frameworks remain focused on individual behaviour. Multidimensional poverty is a plausible structural determinant of brain health but is rarely assessed. Methods: This cross-sectional analysis of the community-based Akili Mali study assessed adults aged 60 years and older in three rural communities in Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. Outcomes were the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), IDEA cognitive screen, CERAD ten-word list, and verbal fluency. Deprivation was measured with a nine-indicator Alkire-Foster Multidimensional Deprivation Index. Missing data were multiply imputed; models adjusted for age, sex, education, community, comorbidity, and health behaviours. Results: Of 1054 participants (mean age 70.2 years [SD 9.35]; 629 [59.7%] women), 840 (81.9%) of 1026 were multidimensionally deprived. Each unit increase in deprivation score predicted a higher GDS-15 score ({beta} 4.83, 95% CI 3.82 to 5.83), higher odds of screen-positive depression (odds ratio 17.18, 6.89 to 42.83), lower IDEA score ({beta} -1.97, -2.97 to -0.97), and lower verbal fluency ({beta} -2.57, -3.77 to -1.36; all p<0.001). CERAD measures and self-reported impairment showed no association. At community level this gradient inverted: the most deprived community had the lowest depression and highest cognition, yet perceived social standing did not differ. Conclusion: Multidimensional deprivation was near-universal and independently associated with worse brain health. The community-level inversion, with perceived social standing equivalent across communities of unequal material circumstances, indicates that absolute deprivation alone does not explain the distribution of brain health. Relative position and community resilience are priorities for study

papers.title: The life course shaping of quality of life in older age: does childhood poverty associate with control, autonomy, self-realisation and pleasure? A retrospective and prospective study of HRS, ELSA, SHARE and TILDA cohorts
papers.abstract: Later-life quality of life is increasingly recognised as a life-course achievement, yet ageing research has focused more on dysfunction and decline than on positive wellbeing. This study examines whether childhood poverty shapes later-life quality of life, measured by CASP: control, autonomy, self-realisation and pleasure. METHODS: I analysed harmonised data from 59,569 adults aged over 50 in 29 countries, drawn from HRS, ELSA, SHARE and TILDA (U.S. Health and Retirement Study, English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe, The Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing). Childhood poverty was modelled as a latent class from retrospectively reported childhood material circumstances, acknowledging recall error in such reports. Country fixed-effects linear models estimated associations with CASP, first adjusting for age, sex and country, then adding education, marital status and later-life wealth. RESULTS: One in five participants grew up in poverty (22.9%). Mean CASP was 38 out of 48. Initially childhood poverty was associated with a 1.2-point lower CASP score; after complete adjustment the penalty attenuated but remained durable at 0.7 points. Education, partnership and wealth were independently associated with higher wellbeing but did not erase the penalty. Predicted age profiles showed poverty penalty in every country. They also revealed striking national differences: Nordic countries achieved markedly higher CASP levels than several Eastern European countries; Finns aged 90 had similar levels of positive wellbeing to Latvians two decades younger. CONCLUSION: Childhood poverty leaves a durable mark on later-life positive wellbeing, while welfare contexts appear to lift overall CASP levels. Reducing child poverty and strengthening social protection are therefore lifelong wellbeing policies.

papers.title: Wastewater pathogen composition in Atlanta, GA prior to and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
papers.abstract: Mass gatherings can have many impacts on public health, including facilitating the spread of infectious diseases. Alternative surveillance modalities, such as wastewater-based surveillance (WBS), can complement traditional clinical surveillance. We utilized WBS to examine the influence of the 2026 FIFA World Cup (FWC'26) on the range of infectious pathogens in Atlanta, GA surrounding matches held in the city. Samples (n = 102) were collected from three water reclamation facilities between April and July of 2026 (34 collection days) and tested using the BIOFIRE(R) WATCHFIRE Respiratory (19 targets) and Gastrointestinal (22 targets) PCR Pathogen Panels. Primary data analysis included a temporal comparison of wastewater pathogen profiles before (April 1 to June 10; n = 60) and during (June 15 to July 15; n = 30) the FWC'26 across the three facilities using a modified Poisson model with Bonferroni correction. There were no statistically significant differences in target detection between the two periods. Samples collected after the FWC'26 (July 20 to 29; n = 12) were included in a sensitivity analysis which showed a statistically significant increase in SARS-CoV-2 (RR = 3.21, 95% CI = 1.40-7.39; p = 0.01, p-adjusted = 0.048) during and after the tournament compared to before. However, this coincided with regional and national increases in SARS-CoV-2 detection in wastewater, suggesting ongoing community burden. Wide confidence intervals, lack of quantitative data, and limited data collection after the matches limit our conclusions. This study demonstrates the use of qualitative, multiplexed PCR assays for WBS during a mass gathering sporting event.

papers.title: Epidemiology of acute respiratory infections in adult patients in Hospices Civils de Lyon, France, between October 2016 and April 2025
papers.abstract: Background Multiple viruses can cause acute respiratory infections (ARI), impacting morbidity, mortality and hospital resources. The objective of this study was to describe viral circulation among patients with ARI, patients characteristics and severity outcomes. Methods A retrospective cohort was assembled using electronic health records from the Hospices Civils de Lyon, France. Adult patients ([≥]18 years) hospitalised or presenting to the emergency department from October 2016 to April 2025 with either an ICD-10 diagnostic code for ARI or a laboratory-confirmed viral detection were included. Administrative variables and laboratory results collected during the stay were extracted. Results 103,011 hospital visits involving 82,077 patients were included. The number of eligible stays increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic, along with year-round laboratory testing. Following disruption during the pandemic, winter peaks of ARI incidence, influenza and RSV detections re-emerged after 2022. Influenza, rhinovirus and SARS-CoV-2 positivity rates peaked in younger adults (<65 years), whereas RSV and hMPV positivity rates were highest in patients aged [≥]80 years. Patients aged [≥]65 years had longer hospitalisations (median 10 vs 8 days, p<0.001), twice in-hospital mortality rate (14% vs 7%, p<0.001), less frequent ICU admission (21% vs 33%, p<0.001) and use of respiratory support than younger adults. Influenza was the virus associated with the shortest length of stays, hMPV was associated with the longest in younger adults. Conclusions Real-world hospital data are valuable for surveillance of viral circulation, early identification of patients at risk of deterioration, and may be used to evaluate the impact of preventive intervention in community.

papers.title: Estimated impacts of mandatory sodium reformulation targets on sodium consumption, health outcomes, health sector costs and health equity in Aotearoa New Zealand
papers.abstract: Aims Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), including for M[a]ori, the Indigenous population. Sodium intake is a modifiable CVD risk factor. In 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) released sodium reduction benchmarks for 58 packaged food categories. We aimed to estimate the health, health-sector cost, and equity impacts of mandating these benchmarks in NZ. Methods Nationally representative data on household food purchases, packaged food sodium content, and dietary intake were used to estimate baseline sodium consumption (2011) and changes following implementation of the WHO benchmarks. A dietary multi-state life-table model estimated impacts on health-adjusted life years (HALYs) and health system costs (2011 NZ$, 3% discount rate) over the remaining lifetime of the 2011 NZ population (n = 4.4 million). Analyses examined impacts by sex and for M[a]ori. Results Mandatory reformulation was estimated to reduce sodium intake by 470 mg/day per person (1.18 g salt), a 22% reduction from baseline. Across population groups, age-standardised reductions ranged from 380 to 660 mg/day (22-23%), generating an estimated 55,600 HALYs (95% uncertainty interval 19,100-90,000) and NZ$535.2 million in health-system cost savings (95% UI: 183.0-914.6 million) over the population lifetime. M[a]ori gained 11,600 HALYs (95% UI: 4,900-17,700), equivalent to 17.2 HALYs per 1,000 population, compared with 11.8 per 1,000 among non-M[a]ori. Conclusion Mandating WHO sodium benchmarks in NZ could substantially reduce sodium intake, improve population health, reduce health sector costs, and advance health equity. Findings support adoption of this strategy in Aotearoa NZ.

papers.title: Who leads Marburg virus research? Gender, geography and funding in authorship, 2008 to early 2023: a bibliometric baseline before the 2023-2025 outbreaks
papers.abstract: Introduction. Between 2023 and 2025, Marburg virus disease reached Equatorial Guinea, Tanzania, Rwanda and Ethiopia for the first time. WHO's 2025 Marburg research priorities make leadership of studies by local scientists a continuing goal. This study describes who led Marburg virus research before these outbreaks. Methods. I analysed 684 English-language Web of Science papers on Marburg virus published from 2008 to February 2023 (5,700 authorships). Gender was inferred from first names with Gender-API, papers about African countries were identified from their text, funders were harmonised by country and type, and themes were mapped to the WHO priorities. I used Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and logistic and negative binomial regression. Results. Women held 35.1% (95% CI 33.9-36.4) of authorships, 41.6% (37.9-45.4) of first-author and 19.6% (16.7-22.9) of last-author positions. Women last authors rose from 15.1% (2008-2012) to 23.2% (2018-2023). Only 14.6% of papers had an author based in Africa. Of 102 papers about an African country, 25.5% (18.0-34.7) had a first author and 23.5% (16.4-32.6) a last author from that country, below benchmarks for infectious-disease research in Africa. Women based in Africa were last author on 2 papers. Of funded papers, 69.0% acknowledged a US funder (24.0% a US defence agency) and 3.2% an African funder. WHO priorities on clinical care, outbreak trials, social science and capacity strengthening each appeared in fewer than 8% of papers. An apparent citation penalty for funded papers disappeared after adjustment (rate ratio 1.07, 0.87-1.33). Conclusions. Before the recent outbreaks, Marburg virus research was led mostly by men in senior positions and by researchers outside the affected countries, and was funded mainly by US agencies. This baseline can track whether recent African-led responses change who leads the field.

papers.title: Peak Agricultural Pesticide Spray Periods are related to Real-World Cognition Using an Ecological Momentary Assessment Burst Design over Two Years
papers.abstract: Objective: Emerging evidence suggests that exposure to organophosphate, neonicotinoid, and other pesticides may transiently impair cognition; however, traditional "snapshot" laboratory-based cognitive assessments fail to capture fluctuations in cognitive performance. This study used ecological momentary cognitive testing (EMCT) to evaluate whether real-world cognitive performance differs between peak and low floricultural pesticide spray seasons, thereby evaluating the potential cyclical effects of agricultural production and related pesticide exposures. Material and Methods: From 2022 to 2024, 15,063 EMCT assessments were completed by 494 participants (ages 17 to 25; 50% female) enrolled in the ESPINA cohort study in Ecuador. Participants completed nine 10-day burst assessments every 2 to 3 months during high and low pesticide spray seasons. EMCTs (NeuroUx) assessed processing speed, executive function, and visual working memory. Mixed-effects models examined associations of peak versus off-peak pesticide spray seasons, floricultural work or occupation (vs not) with EMCT performance, adjusting for socio-economic and other variables, and including participant- and burst-level random intercepts. Results: Peak pesticide spray season, compared to off-peak, was associated with higher T-scores on processing speed tests, including Matching Pair (B= 0.62) and Odd One Out (B= 0.88), but showed no significant association with other tests or the overall cognitive composite. Conversely, direct floricultural employment was significantly associated with lower cognitive performance overall (B= -0.59), with the largest differences observed in Memory Matrix (B= -0.78) and Matching Pair (B= -0.70). Conclusion: Peak pesticide spray seasons were associated with modestly higher processing speed scores, consistent with prior findings in this population suggestive of enhanced cognitive performance associated with neonicotinoid and sulfoximine exposures. In contrast, floricultural employment was associated with significantly lower memory and overall cognitive performance. These results suggest that occupational and seasonal pesticide exposure may have distinct associations with cognitive functioning, highlighting the importance of repeated cognitive testing for characterizing potentially transient effects.

papers.title: Place-based structural disadvantage and mortality inequality across 379 Polish counties, 2010-2025: a spatial Mundlak analysis
papers.abstract: Place-based mortality inequalities may persist even as short-term associations with local conditions change. We examined age-sex-standardised all-cause mortality in 379 harmonised Polish counties (2010-2025), asking whether durable between-county differences or lagged within-county deviations better characterise mortality geography. Spatial Mundlak generalised additive models allowed non-linear associations and county-specific spatial modification; a pre-COVID model (2010-2019) was compared with overlapping models through 2022 and 2025. In the pre-COVID model, median county average partial slopes per standard deviation were -26.1 deaths per 100,000 for higher education, +29.4 for primary/lower-secondary education and +30.2 for PM2.5. Directions of these between-county gradients persisted across analytical windows. By contrast, within-county associations were less stable and sometimes reversed sign in pandemic-inclusive models. County-level uncertainty indicated stronger and more coherent pre-COVID spatial patterns for education, PM2.5 and population density than for several health-care and migration terms. Strict leave-one-year-out validation revealed weak temporal transportability, particularly for the 2010-2022 model, limiting predictive interpretation. Outcome-defined comparisons further showed that educational composition remained an important separator of high- and low-mortality counties after COVID-19, while the fitted PM2.5 contribution contrast diminished. These findings distinguish durable configurations of place-based disadvantage from period-dependent ecological co-movement. They support geographically sensitive, multi-domain approaches to reducing mortality inequalities, while not establishing individual-level causal effects.

papers.title: Utility of Rt epidemic trend categories for influenza surveillance: alignment with observed emergency department trends across two influenza seasons in the United States
papers.abstract: CDC has estimated the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for influenza in the United States since 2023, translating the posterior probability that Rt exceeds one, P(R_t>1), into epidemic trend categories (growing, likely growing, not changing, likely declining, declining). If Rt reliably indicates infection dynamics, growing or declining trends should precede corresponding changes in influenza-related emergency department (ED) visits, accounting for the lag between infection and care-seeking. However, because these categories reflect confidence in the direction of change rather than magnitude, their alignment with the corresponding trends ED activity measures is unclear. We compared weekly Rt epidemic trend categories to observed ED trends from the National Syndromic Surveillance Program across the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza seasons, using three thresholds to define observed trends at different magnitudes ([≥]0.1% difference, [≥]0.5% difference, [≥]5% relative change between consecutive weeks), comparing Rt trends to observed trends the following week. We assessed categorical alignment and calibration between P(R_t>1) and observed trends. Alignment was moderate overall, strongest for growing and declining categories under the 5% relative change threshold (61% aligned) and weakest under the 0.5% difference threshold (38.2% aligned); calibration was similarly best under the 5% relative change threshold. Misalignment concentrated around epidemic inflection points and periods of low influenza activity. Rt epidemic trend categories showed moderate, threshold-dependent alignment with observed ED activity, reflecting a combination of real-time model error and misalignment between direction-based and magnitude-based surveillance metrics. Defining categories based on Rt magnitude could improve correspondence with size-based change indicators and strengthen their utility for real-time monitoring.

papers.title: From telling to receiving: the disclosure-and-services cascade after childhood sexual abuse across 15 low- and middle-income countries
papers.abstract: Most children who experience sexual abuse in low- and middle-income countries never receive formal help, but few studies have followed survivors through the steps from telling someone to receiving services. In this pooled cross-sectional analysis, we combined 15 nationally representative Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS) fielded between 2013 and 2024 in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe to describe this disclosure-and-services cascade and the factors associated with each step. The analytic sample comprised 3,608 respondents aged 18-24 years who reported sexual abuse before age 18 (2,852 female, 756 male). We estimated survey-weighted proportions for four steps: told anyone, knew where to seek formal help, sought help (among those who knew), and received help (among those who sought it). Design-based logistic regression with country fixed effects estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for individual, family, and community factors. Overall, 47.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 44.4-49.7) of survivors had told anyone and 34.8% (32.2-37.5) knew where to seek formal help. Of those who knew (n = 1,208), 24.8% (20.9-29.1) sought help, and of those who sought help (n = 339), 81.9% (75.9-86.7) received it. In total, 7.0% (5.7-8.5) of survivors received formal help; this proportion ranged from 0.9% to 26.3% across countries. Compared with male survivors, female survivors were more likely to tell anyone (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.73-3.05) and less likely to know where to seek help (aOR 0.68, 0.50-0.93); among survivors who knew where to go, female survivors were more likely to seek help (aOR 2.66, 1.39-5.09). Knowing where to seek help was more likely with older age, more schooling, and a living mother. Survivors who had ever married or cohabited were less likely to have told anyone (aOR 0.75, 0.58-0.96). No factor other than sex was associated with seeking help among those who knew where to go. Most survivors are lost before they reach a service: two in three do not know where to go, and three in four of those who know ultimately do not seek help. Once survivors seek help, most receive it. Interventions should make services known to young people, particularly those with less schooling, and address the barriers that keep survivors, especially young men, from using services they know about.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to tick awareness and prevention among users of urban green spaces: insights from stakeholder focus groups
papers.abstract: BackgroundTicks in the UK can transmit pathogens that lead to diseases in humans, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Expanding tick populations and increasing human use of urban green spaces may elevate exposure risk. Public health advice exists, but little is known about how this guidance is understood and applied by users of urban environments. MethodsFour stakeholder focus groups were conducted with professionals involved in tick fieldwork in urban green spaces. Discussions explored interactions with the public, perceived awareness, behaviours, and views on communication. Data were analysed thematically using an approach informed by the Framework Method. ResultsStakeholders reported substantial variation in public awareness of ticks, influenced by prior exposure to rural environments and local knowledge. Misinformation, particularly around tick removal, was common. Signage was rarely observed in urban green spaces, and views on its effectiveness were mixed. Participants emphasised the need to balance risk communication with reassurance and highlighted the importance of age-appropriate education. ConclusionsInsights from stakeholders underline the importance of targeted, context-specific public health messaging in urban settings. Priorities include identifying groups with lower awareness, addressing misinformation, designing balanced communication materials, evaluating the effectiveness of signage, and integrating education for children and families.

papers.title: Applying Diagnostic Network Optimisation analysis to inform the introduction of G6PD testing into Indonesia for improved treatment of relapsing malaria
papers.abstract: Background: Radical cure for P. vivax and P. ovale malaria using 8-aminoquinoline drugs primaquine or tafenoquine can prevent relapse, but requires glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) screening due to the risk of haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals. This study aimed to provide an evidence-based framework to inform the optimal allocation and referral networks for G6PD testing devices in Indonesia. Methods: A diagnostic network optimisation (DNO) analysis using OptiDx was conducted across eight districts in Sumba, North Sumatra, and Central Java, representing high-, moderate-, and low-transmission settings. The maximum annual number of malaria cases from surveillance data between 2019 and 2022 was used as a proxy for testing demand. In baseline scenario, all public health facilities were equipped with G6PD testing devices. In referral scenario, devices were allocated only to selected facilities, with a maximum sample transport distance of 15 kilometres and sample delivery scheduled three times per week. Model outputs were reviewed with the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) to identify the optimal scenario, considering factors including implementation cost and accessibility. Results: Equipping 39% (30/76) of facilities in Sumba with G6PD testing devices could reduce total costs by nearly 30% in the first year and approximately 20% in subsequent years compared with the baseline, although the average referral distance increased from 4.48 kilometres to 9.8 kilometres. In North Sumatra, deploying 15 of 68 devices (19%) could reduce total costs by almost 60% in the first year and approximately 15% thereafter. Two health facilities (Puskesmas Padewatu in Sumba and Abdul Manan Hospital in North Sumatra) could experience workload increase exceeding 400 hours annually as referral facilities. In Purworejo, a single device placed at Puskesmas Mranti could enable on-site diagnosis for 56% of patients. Interpretation: The findings demonstrated that DNO can identify cost-efficient and equitable G6PD testing strategies to support safe radical cure and accelerate malaria elimination.

papers.title: Validation of the PACER-PT: a measure of health-relevant perceptions of gentrification-related neighbourhood change
papers.abstract: Objective: Urban neighbourhoods across Europe are rapidly transforming through gentrification, with Portuguese cities particularly affected. Although the health impacts of these changes are increasingly recognised, validated instruments to assess perceptions of neighbourhood change remain scarce. This study adapted and validated a Portuguese version of the Perceptions About Change in Environment and Residents (PACER-PT) scale. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 255 adults living for >=5yrs in the Lisbon and Porto Metropolitan Areas. PACER was translated and culturally adapted to create PACER-PT. We evaluated psychometric properties using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), internal consistency, and convergent and criterion validity. Results: EFA identified a three-factor structure explaining 47.5% of the variance: Built, social and economic changes, Positive attitude towards neighbourhood changes, and Displacement concerns and neighbourhood disruption. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach s alpha=0.70-0.78). Convergent/criterion validity were supported by significant associations with amount and pace of change, self-rated health, and quality of life. Younger and wealthier participants and those with greater residential satisfaction reported more favourable perceptions. Conclusions: PACER-PT demonstrated it is a valid instrument for assessing gentrification-related neighbourhood changes in Portugal.

papers.title: The impact of warning labels versus traffic light labels on food choice and negative emotional responses: two randomised controlled trials among UK adult populations with and without an eating disorder
papers.abstract: BackgroundIn the UK, front-of-pack traffic light labels (TLL) are implemented voluntarily. The UK Government are considering alternative FOP approaches, such as nutrient warning labels (WL). However, the effects and potential harm of TLL versus WL in UK consumers are unclear. We compared the effects of WL, TLL, and no label on unhealthy food item selection and negative affect among UK adults with and without an eating disorder (ED). MethodsWe conducted two online randomised controlled trials. In Study 1, 924 UK adults without an ED diagnosis were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to a WL, TLL, or no labels condition and completed a food-choice task. In Study 2, 240 UK adults with an ED diagnosis completed a baseline no-label food choice task and were subsequently randomly assigned (1:1:1) to WL, TLL, or no labels for a follow-up food choice task. The primary outcome was the number of task-specific unhealthy food items selected. Negative affect before and after food choice tasks was measured as a secondary outcome. FindingsIn Study 1 (data collected 02/25 - 04/25), unhealthy food selection differed by condition (p = .013). Of five products selected, WL participants selected 0.20 fewer unhealthy items than TLL participants (8.0%; p = .038) and 0.28 fewer than controls (10.7%; p = .004). In Study 2 (data collected 11/25 - 02/26), unhealthy selection decreased by 0.39 items with WL (17.7%; p = .015), 0.13 with TLL (5.3%, p = .286), and 0.00 with no labels. The reduction was greater with WL than with no labels (p = .029). Label condition did not differentially affect task-related negative affect in either study (Study 1, p = .757; Study 2, p = .448). InterpretationWL tended to be associated with lower unhealthy food selection compared to TLL in UK adults. There was minimal evidence that WL or TLL caused negative emotional responses. FundingThis research was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Oxford Health BRC. The views expressed are those of the author(s) and not necessarily those of the NIHR or the Department of Health and Social Care. RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov NCT07339969

papers.title: Oral rehydration salts and zinc for childhood diarrhoea in Bangladesh, 2019 and 2025: coverage, wealth inequality and reported source of care
papers.abstract: BackgroundDiarrhoea remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five. WHO and UNICEF recommend oral rehydration salts (ORS) alongside 10 to 14 days of zinc supplementation. However, national progress in combined treatment coverage and its socioeconomic and care-related inequalities remains insufficiently understood in Bangladesh. We assessed combined coverage, wealth inequality and differences by reported source of care. MethodsWe analysed children under five with caregiver-reported diarrhoea in the 2019 (n=1,589) and 2025 (n=1,634) Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). We estimated combined coverage using design-based methods, wealth inequality using slope indices, and associations with source of care using pooled adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR). Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimates provided an external comparison. ResultsCombined ORS and zinc coverage increased from 35.0% (95% CI 32.3 to 37.7) in 2019 to 42.9% (40.1 to 45.8) in 2025. In 2025, ORS and zinc coverage were 75.8% and 51.9%, respectively. The 2025 estimate agreed with DHS 2022, whereas MICS 2019 was below DHS 2017-18. Wealth inequality persisted in 2025 (slope index 13.0 percentage points, 3.4 to 22.6). Adjustment attenuated the pooled slope index from 11.8 to 6.5 points (-1.7 to 14.6). Coverage was lower with pharmacy-only than public care (aPR 0.59, 0.53 to 0.66) and with no care reported (0.14, 0.11 to 0.18). Children with no care reported accounted for 43.7% of children without combined treatment in 2025. ConclusionsCombined coverage increased, although the apparent progress may be overstated by the lower MICS 2019 estimate relative to DHS. Zinc remained the larger treatment gap, while one in four children received no ORS. Reported sources of care require cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Serotype-structured force of infection for optimizing dengue vaccine trial design
papers.abstract: Dengue fever, transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti, remains a major global public health threat, causing an estimated 390 million infections annually. Designing efficient dengue vaccine efficacy trials in endemic regions is challenging because transmission intensity varies across space and time, baseline population immunity is heterogeneous, and endpoint accrual depends strongly on the local force of infection (FoI). We developed a simulation framework for trial planning in endemic settings that links FoI to age-specific seroprevalence through a catalytic model and then translates FoI into symptomatic endpoint incidence for randomized controlled trial simulations. Across a range of FoI scenarios representing low-to-high endemic transmission, we evaluated sample size requirements, follow-up duration, and expected power under alternative vaccine efficacy assumptions. In high-transmission settings, the framework indicates that trials enrolling 5,000-10,000 participants per arm can achieve at least 80% power within 12-24 months of follow-up under plausible symptomatic detection assumptions. Sensitivity analyses demonstrate that feasibility thresholds are most sensitive to FoI and the symptomatic fraction, high-lighting the importance of site selection and surveillance intensity. Overall, the proposed FoI-based approach provides practical guidance for dengue trial design, including sample size determination, follow-up planning, and the identification of epidemiological conditions under which vaccine evaluation is most efficient in endemic settings.

papers.title: Maternal mortality risk among Black women in Brazil: a nationwide spatial consensus approach
papers.abstract: Although preventable, maternal mortality remains a global challenge. Its burden is disproportionately concentrated in low- and middle-income settings. Substantial subnational geographical variations also persist within countries, driven by underlying socioeconomic disparities and unequal access to quality healthcare services. Here we propose a spatial consensus framework combining frequentist and Bayesian models to overcome variance instability in small-area estimates, mapping maternal mortality risk among Black women in Brazil to guide equitable public health interventions. Using nationwide surveillance data (2019-2024), we applied a spatial Poisson probability model to detect high-rate clusters of maternal mortality among Black women. Concurrently, Bayesian hierarchical spatial models were fitted to smooth small-area rates and stabilize variance. Results from both approaches were integrated into a five-level risk typology to categorize Brazilian municipalities. National aggregate reductions in Brazilian maternal mortality mask profound, spatially concentrated racial inequities. The spatial classification of risk scenarios identified 13 municipalities with Confirmed Critical Risk, 28 municipalities with Persistent Regional Risk, 12 municipalities with a Local Excess Alert, and 4 exhibiting Epidemiological Silence. The vast majority remained at the Expected Risk Level. The proposed spatial consensus framework translates complex spatio-temporal modeling into an operational typology for surveillance systems. This approach bridges the gap between spatial analytics and public health decision-making, providing a replicable tool to address structural racial disparities in maternal health within decentralized health systems. FundingInstitutional Development Program of the Unified Health System (PROADI-SUS), under protocol number (NUP) 25000.082775/2024-00.

papers.title: Chronic health conditions, multimorbidity and subsequent economic inactivity in three British birth cohorts
papers.abstract: BackgroundEconomic inactivity due to ill-health has been rising in the United Kingdom. Chronic health conditions make up most of the burden of poor health, and frequently co-occur, yet the impact of multimorbidity on economic inactivity remains underexplored. MethodsData was from three British birth cohorts (born in 1946, 1958 and 1970). Psychological distress, chronic back pain and cardiometabolic disease were assessed in participants thirties and forties, and economic inactivity one to two decades later. Modified Poisson regression models with robust standard errors estimated associations between health and inactivity, accounting for economic activity at baseline and several socioeconomic and demographic confounders. We tested for multiplicative and additive interaction between condition pairs. ResultsThe prevalence of all three health conditions increased with age. Each was associated with a higher risk of later economic inactivity in fully adjusted models. Psychological distress was the strongest and most consistent predictor across cohorts (RR = 1.22 (95% CI 0.90-1.64) to 1.99 (95% CI 1.67-2.38)). Comorbidity was common; more than 10% of participants experienced two or more conditions in their forties. Risk of economic inactivity increased with multimorbidity. However, we found little evidence that risk for comorbidity exceeded the sum of individual conditions on either the multiplicative or additive scales. ConclusionsCommon chronic conditions in adulthood, particularly when comorbid, are associated with a substantially higher risk of economic inactivity across decades-long time horizons. This association has persisted over time and across policy contexts.

papers.title: Higher Nocturnal Temperatures Shorten and Worsen Sleep with No Clear Evidence of Short-Term Compensatory Patterns
papers.abstract: Background & ObjectivesRising nighttime temperatures menace sleep, yet evidence from large longitudinal studies combining objective and subjective sleep measures remains limited. Here, we therefore examined associations of nocturnal air and wet-bulb temperature with seven sleep parameters, including possible delayed effects. MethodsWe analysed wearable-derived and subjective sleep data from 326 home-care workers (270 women) in Switzerland between June and Early October 2025, resulting in 14,290 participant-nights. Nocturnal air temperature and humidity data were obtained from the dense MeteoSwiss monitoring network (mean distance from participants homes, 8.6 km). Bayesian multilevel models estimated nonlinear same-night within-person and between-person associations, while exploratory lag models examined whether associations with nocturnal temperature were also evident for exposures one and two nights earlier. ResultsSleep maintenance efficiency, the primary outcome, showed no meaningful association with nocturnal air temperature. In contrast, warmer-than-usual nights were associated with shorter total sleep time and poorer subjective sleep quality. Compared with a participants usual exposure, total sleep time was 13.3 min shorter at +5{degrees}C, while subjective sleep-quality scores worsened by 1.2 points. At +5{degrees}C, the probability of sleeping less than 7 h was 10.6 percentage points higher than at-4{degrees}C relative to a participants usual exposure. Changes in sleep-stage percentages and recovery index were very small. Wet-bulb results were broadly comparable while exploratory lag analyses provided little evidence of consistent delayed effects. ConclusionsHigher nocturnal ambient temperatures were associated with shorter and poorer sleep, with no evidence of short-term compensatory patterns. The results thus underline that sleep disturbances may represent an important pathway linking warming nights to human health.

papers.title: Longitudinal Associations of Cigarette Smoking, Smoking Intensity, and Smoking TrajectoriesWith Emergency Room Utilization Among U.S. Adults
papers.abstract: BackgroundTobacco smoking is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, yet its longitudinal association with emergency room (ER) utilization remains understudied. We examined whether cigarette smoking, smoking intensity, and smoking trajectories were associated with subsequent ER use. MethodsWe analyzed adult respondents from Waves 1-6 of the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study. Wave 1-3 smoking status, intensity, and cigarettes/day were examined in relation to next-wave ER outcomes. Logistic generalized estimating equation models were used for any ER visit and frequent ER use ([≥]2 visits), and quasi-Poisson models were used for ER visit count. Trajectory analyses examined Wave 1-5 smoking patterns and Wave 6 ER outcomes, with Wave 1-4 to Wave 5 as sensitivity analysis. Marginal structural models and propensity score matching were used to strengthen causal interpretation. Models adjusted for demographics, insurance, self-rated health, and baseline ER use. Survey weights with balanced repeated replication and Fays adjustment were used. ResultsIn adjusted GEE models, current smoking was associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, including any ER visit (OR 1.128, 95% CI [1.068-1.191]), frequent ER use (OR 1.275, 95% CI [1.185-1.372]), and ER visit count (RR 1.264, 95% CI [1.160-1.377]; all p<0.001). Smoking intensity showed a dose-response pattern: smoking <20 cigarettes/day was associated with any ER visit (OR 1.130, 95% CI [1.060-1.204]), frequent ER use (OR 1.231, 95% CI [1.124-1.347]), and ER visit count (RR 1.262, 95% CI [1.110-1.435]), while smoking[≥] 20 cigarettes/day showed stronger associations with any ER visit (OR 1.231, 95% CI [1.127-1.345]), frequent ER use (OR 1.447, 95% CI [1.293-1.618]), and ER visit count (RR 1.368, 95% CI [1.245-1.504]; all p<0.001). Each additional cigarette/day was also associated with higher ER utilization (OR/RR range, 1.007- 1.011; all p<0.001). Findings were consistent in marginal structural models and propensity score matched analyses. In trajectory analyses, new/intermittent and persistent smokers had significantly higher ER utilization, while former/intermittent smokers and sustained quitters did not differ from non-smokers, suggesting that this harmful association was eliminated by smoking cessation. ConclusionsSmoking, heavier intensity, and persistent or emerging smoking patterns were associated with higher subsequent ER utilization, while smoking cessation reduces ER risk to the same level as non-smokers. This supports smoking prevention and cessation as strategies to reduce acute healthcare burden. IMPLICATIONSSmoking should be considered not only a risk factor for long-term chronic disease, but also a predictor of acute healthcare utilization. The consistency of findings across longitudinal, marginal structural, and propensity score matched analyses supports a potential causal relationship between smoking exposure and subsequent emergency room use. These results strengthen the rationale for integrating smoking cessation counseling, nicotine replacement therapy, quitline referral, and preventive care linkage into emergency and urgent care settings, alongside broader tobacco-control policies to reduce acute healthcare burden.

papers.title: Constructing expert models of adolescent vaping behaviour: A mental models study
papers.abstract: Research on vaping prevention messages has predominantly examined adolescents perceptions of and responses and the research exploring how experts perspectives is limited. Expert knowledge is crucial for conceptualising the risk phenomenon and its key causal mechanisms, uncertainties, and issues that are relevant to address in evidence-based communication strategies. This study therefore explored how professionals and experts conceptualise and understand adolescent vaping behaviour, including its perceived causes and drivers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with a purposive sample of 12 experts from medical research, addiction science, public health prevention, and adolescent-oriented practice in Norway. Data collection and analysis were informed by the mental models approach to risk communication. The analysis identified an expert-derived mental model/influence diagram of adolescent vaping behaviour. Across expert domains, vaping was understood as a multifactorial phenomenon emerging from interacting biological, psychological, and social factors operating across multiple system levels. The first theme describes vaping initiation as a socially embedded and often intermittent practice shaped by identity development, peer belonging, and low perceived harm. The second theme captures how vaping is enabled, sustained, and legitimised through interacting drivers operating across social, structural, commercial, and regulatory contexts. The third theme focuses on reinforcement processes, whereby nicotine dependence and emotional coping mechanisms contribute to more sustained use. According to these expert accounts, adolescent vaping is sustained and legitimised through broader processes of normalisation operating across multiple societal levels. The expert perspectives identified in this study suggest that comparative risk framings of e-cigarettes as less harmful than cigarettes, and the social functions of vaping within adolescent peer cultures, may be important considerations in the development of risk communication targeting adolescents.

papers.title: Extending Problem and Solution Trees: A Participatory Method for Community Partnership Development
papers.abstract: BackgroundProblem and solution trees (PASTs) are a participatory method for understanding complex environmental and systemic health problems and incorporating community input in appropriate solutions. While PASTs have been applied in international contexts to examine critical health concerns (e.g., hand-washing behaviors and malnutrition), their use in the United States (US) is limited. ObjectivesTogether with a Project Advisory Board (PAB), identify barriers to DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) eating plan adoption and co-develop actionable solutions to low adherence for a historically marginalized community in the U.S. MethodsPASTs are visual tools. Over virtual and in-person meetings, we constructed and refined five distinct trees to address each core barrier to DASH adherence. We made real-time edits to trees in PowerPoint and engaged in group discussion to reach consensus on barriers and solutions. Supporting material included a project workbook distributed to the PAB. Meetings were audio-recorded, and transcripts were reviewed following each meeting to ensure the accuracy of each tree. The PAST method aided collaboration with the PAB by allowing members to identify additional barriers and refine the trees based on their knowledge and experience. PASTs additionally supported the community-engaged partnership by identifying the interconnectedness of core problems (i.e., limited supply of healthy foods and preference for salty foods). ConclusionsPASTs showed their relevance as tools for community-engaged research and responsive program planning. Challenges in creating and presenting intricate trees via online format highlight considerations for virtual facilitation and real-time documentation. Adaptations to the method are described for future use.

papers.title: The Story of Shukuru - a film to enhance knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding schistosomiasis and related elimination interventions in Pemba, Tanzania.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSchistosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease affecting individuals in 79 countries, primarily in sub-Saharan Africa. The World Health Organization recommends the treatment, snail control, and behavior change interventions to decrease prevalence, but culturally tailored interventions remain rare. Here we aim to determine the impact of an educational film on schistosomiasis-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among schoolchildren and adults in Pemba, Tanzania. Methodology/Principal FindingsFrom November 2023 to February 2024, a survey was conducted among adult community members in 20 administrative areas in Pemba on their preferences for a planned film about schistosomiasis. The film was produced in March 2024 based on these suggestions and filmed in Pemba. In July 2024, a pretest-posttest study in ten administrative areas assessed the films impact on schistosomiasis-related knowledge, attitudes, and willingness to change behavior among children and adults. Binomial generalized linear mixed-effects models estimated changes in knowledge and attitudes before versus after viewing. Of 882 participants surveyed in 2023/24, 810 (91.8%) were willing to watch a film about schistosomiasis, most commonly on TV (545, 67.3%). The impact study included 195 children and 195 adults. The odds of a correct knowledge answer were 39% higher after viewing (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.29-1.50, p<0.001), and the odds of a positive attitude were 77% higher (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.47-2.12, p<0.001). Before the film, 71.9% (200/278) of participants used natural water bodies for daily activities, and 72.5% (145/200) of these never used protective clothing. Afterward, 88.2% (240/272) reported being likely to avoid water bodies and 54.4% (148/272) likely to use protective clothing. Conclusions/SignificanceAn educational film developed from community input and filmed locally increased knowledge and attitudes among children and adults and fostered willingness to adopt self-protective behaviors. However, willingness alone is insufficient without infrastructure (e.g., wells, tap water) to change behavior. Therefore, such investments remain essential for schistosomiasis elimination. Author SummarySchistosomiasis is a disease caused by parasitic worms that live in open freshwater bodies, and it affects people in many countries, most heavily in sub-Saharan Africa. People become infected through everyday contact with contaminated water, such as swimming, washing, or farming. The World Health Organization recommends treatment, snail control and behavior change to reduce the disease, but most educational efforts are not tailored to local culture. We worked with communities on the island of Pemba, Tanzania, to create an educational film about schistosomiasis, shaped by residents own ideas about what such a film should look like and where they would watch it. We then tested whether the film changed peoples knowledge, attitudes, and stated intentions around water contact, comparing childrens and adults responses before and after watching. Knowledge and positive attitudes both improved after viewing, and many participants said they intended to avoid risky water contact and use protective items such as rubber boots. However, good intentions are not enough on their own: without safer alternatives like wells or tap water stations, people may have no real choice but to keep using open water bodies. Eliminating schistosomiasis will require investment in this kind of infrastructure alongside education.

papers.title: Assessing HIV vulnerability among young women in South Africa: A comparison of three risk assessment tools
papers.abstract: BackgroundYoung women in sub-Saharan Africa remain disproportionately affected by HIV. However, self-perceived HIV risk may not align with reported sexual behaviors or other dimensions of risk. Behavioral measures, such as the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), may capture risk-taking propensity not reflected in conventional self-report measures. We compared self-perceived HIV risk, behavior-based HIV risk, and behavioral risk-taking propensity among young women in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional survey between July and November 2025 among self-reported HIV-negative women aged 18-30 years in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. We assessed self-perceived HIV risk using the Perceived Risk of HIV Scale (PRHS), behavior-based HIV risk using the Vaginal and Oral Interventions to Control the Epidemic (VOICE) Risk Score, and behavioral risk-taking propensity using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART). Spearmans rank correlation coefficients were used to examine correlations between the three measures. ResultsAmong 250 participants, median age was 22 years (IQR 20-25), all identified as Black, and 53.6% were attending school or college. Overall, 42.0% were classified as high risk by VOICE, 6.0% by PRHS, and 33.1% of participants with complete BART data were in the highest tertile of risk-taking propensity. Mean age differed across VOICE categories (p = 0.036), but not PRHS (p = 0.111) or BART categories (p = 0.698). PRHS categories were associated with anal intercourse, oral intercourse, consistent condom use, ever having sold sex, and age-disparate partnerships (all p 0.05). ConclusionsThese findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between reported HIV risk behaviours, perceived HIV risk, and behavioural risk-taking propensity when assessing HIV vulnerability among young women. For HIV prevention programmes, reliance on a single measure may not adequately capture the different dimensions of vulnerability. Integrating behavioural assessments with discussions of perceived risk and individual circumstances may help inform more responsive, person-centred HIV prevention services, including PrEP counselling. Further research is needed to establish how these measures can best complement one another in prevention service delivery.

papers.title: Integrating 16S and 18S sequencing reveals coupled prokaryotic and eukaryotic relationships in drinking water biofilms
papers.abstract: Drinking water biofilms host diverse communities spanning all realms of life. However, despite the known interactions between opportunistic pathogens and microbial eukaryotes such as amoebae, most studies focus only on the prokaryotic populations in these systems. As a result, the degree to which microbial eukaryotes shape biofilm communities and the persistence of opportunistic waterborne pathogens, such as Legionella spp. is still largely unknown. Here we leveraged a set of 128 non-disinfected drinking water shower hose biofilms collected across Switzerland to characterize both communities and quantify eukaryotes role in shaping prokaryotic communities and Legionella persistence. We found both communities to present a conserved set of core taxa dominated by oligotrophic bacterial families and amoebae. The prevalence of taxa was mainly driven by the phylogenetic diversity among their sequence variants rather than their number alone. We detected prokaryotic and eukaryotic communities to show similar patterns in their richness and composition, influencing each other more than abiotic building-level factors. Legionellaceae bacteria were detected in 82% of samples presenting a diversity extending known reference species and no clear dominant taxa. Legionellaceae richness did not correlate with the richness of known amoebal hosts, but rather other amoebae, indicating that eukaryotic taxa relevant for Legionella persistence extend beyond the classically described hosts. These findings highlight the importance of integrating the eukaryotic communities to understand the microbial ecology in drinking water biofilms and recognize the conditions which allow opportunistic waterborne pathogens such as Legionella to persist.

papers.title: Decomposing the Caesarean section trend in Bangladesh (2012-2025): A multivariate Linear Probability Model analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundWhile Caesarean section is a life-saving intervention when medically indicated, the World Health Organization recommends an optimal population-level rate of 10% to 15% to prevent iatrogenic morbidities. In Bangladesh, however, rapid clinical integration within a commercialized, dual-practice healthcare architecture has coincided with an unprecedented escalation in surgical deliveries. Because standard cross-sectional models cannot algebraically separate population shifts from changing provider propensity, this study aimed to decompose the compositional and behavioral drivers of the Caesarean section surge in Bangladesh between 2012 and 2025. MethodsNationally representative data were analyzed from the 2012-2013, 2019, and 2024-2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), comprising 26,534 women aged 15-49 years who delivered a child within the preceding two years. Survey skip-logic was harmonized to retain unmedicalized cohorts receiving zero antenatal care (ANC). A survey-weighted multivariate Linear Probability Model (LPM) Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition was applied to a complete-case cohort (N=16,179) to partition the prevalence change into population-level compositional shifts (endowments) and behavioral changes (coefficients). ResultsNational Caesarean section prevalence surged by 32.47 percentage points, rising from 19.48% in 2012 to 36.05% in 2019 and 51.95% in 2025 (p<0.001). Surgical delivery multiplied over sixfold among the poorest wealth quintile (5.53% to 34.37%), rose by 34.83 percentage points among rural mothers (15.66% to 50.49%), and reached 85.12% within private facilities. Multivariate decomposition demonstrated that 87.77% of the overall increase was attributable to compositional shifts rather than behavioral factors (12.23%). The sharp reduction in pregnancies receiving zero ANC visits (35.52% to 8.12%) independently drove 49.04% of the surge, while increased utilization of private clinics and NGOs (18.20% to 54.36%) explained 43.39%. Conversely, biological indications such as fetal macrosomia contributed less than 1%. ConclusionsThe unprecedented escalation of Caesarean sections in Bangladesh represents a profound pattern of systemic over-medicalization that is independent of baseline clinical risk. The surge is overwhelmingly structural, driven by the disproportionate concentration of deliveries within the commercialized private healthcare sector and supplier-induced demand following integration into formal clinical pathways. Reversing this trajectory necessitates immediate regulatory intervention, specifically the mandate of clinical auditing frameworks such as the Robson classification, to decouple financial incentives from obstetric decision-making in private facilities.

papers.title: Objective sleep tracking for fatigue management in cargo pilots: six months of continuous smart-ring monitoring
papers.abstract: Aviation fatigue management estimates crew sleep from rosters and self-report. We examined how sleep duration changes around flights and with departure and landing times. In an observational cohort study, 13 cargo pilots wore an Ultrahuman smart ring for six months in 2026. We linked 1,504 sleep sessions to the flown schedule. Linear mixed-effects models compared each sleep session with the same pilots rest nights, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Total sleep time was 48 min shorter on the night before a flight (95% CI 32 to 65 min) and 28 min shorter in the first sleep after one (95% CI 13 to 43 min). Later nights did not differ. Sleep duration varied with clock time. Compared with evening departures and landings, respectively, pilots slept 57 min less before a departure between 06:00h and 11:59h (95% CI 14 to 101 min) and 97 min less after a landing between 00:00h and 05:59h (95% CI 37 to 156 min). Flight direction and length showed no association. Differences between pilots explained 14.1% of the variance in total sleep time, more than six times the 2.2% explained by duty position. Fatigue risk management could plan rest around departure and landing times.

papers.title: "It Just Puts You Out!" Tranq Sleep, Sensory Discernment, and the Experience of Consuming Xylazine-Adulterated Fentanyl in Rural North Carolina
papers.abstract: BackgroundXylazine, a veterinary sedative not approved for human use, has emerged as a consequential adulterant in the U.S. illicit fentanyl supply. Although a growing body of qualitative research has documented the experiences of fentanyl consumers exposed to tranq in large Northeastern cities, little is known about how xylazine is experienced in rural or Southern regions where the evolution of the illicit drug supply often lags behind its urban equivalents. This study examines how fentanyl consumers in west-central North Carolina detect, comprehend and respond to the widespread adulteration of fentanyl markets with xylazine. MethodsBetween September and December of 2025, a seasoned interviewer conducted 25 in-depth, semi-structured qualitative interviews with fentanyl consumers recruited from both fixed and mobile syringe service programs in west-central North Carolina. Interviews explored sensory discernment strategies, pharmacologic effects, and behavioral responses to the presence of xylazine. Data were analyzed using a combined deductive-inductive thematic approach in QSR NVivo 14.0. ResultsParticipants described a distinctive repertoire of sensory strategies for identifying xylazine in their fentanyl supply, including the appearance of drug residue on foil, bitterness and chemical odor when smoked, and altered viscosity when injected. A minority described an inability to detect xylazine through sensory cues. Participants consistently distinguished a profound involuntary sedation they called "tranq sleep" from the familiar opioid nod, characterizing it by nearly instantaneous loss of consciousness with severe withdrawal upon awakening. While nearly all participants expressed strong aversion to xylazine, a meaningful minority valued its amplifying effects to improve a diminishing fentanyl high. ConclusionsThis study offers among the first qualitative description of xylazine exposure in a rural fentanyl market. Findings extend the xylazine literature geographically and pharmacologically and underscore the urgency of harm reduction responses tailored to the distinctive harms of xylazine. In particular, adverse health outcomes that accumulate during episodes of protracted and unarousable sedation, including physical injury, victimization, and the severe withdrawal syndrome that follows upon awakening. Highlightsxylazine; tranq sleep, fentanyl; qualitative methods; harm reduction; rural drug markets; drug discernment
